The Laoshan District Land and Resources Bureau's claim that its act of granting the disputed land violated relevant administrative management regulations and required improving tender, auction, or listing procedures, thus making it impossible to continue performing the "State-owned Land Use Rights Grant Contract," pertains to the modification or termination of the relevant contract and affects whether the contract can be actually performed and whether it should be terminated, but does not affect or restrict the validity of the contract and is not a reason or basis for determining the contract as invalid.

Based on the effective criminal judgment (2004) Tai Xing Er Chu Zi No. 20 rendered by the Tai'an Intermediate People's Court of Shandong Province on January 13, 2005, which was provided by the Laoshan District Land and Resources Bureau, it was determined that Lu Guoqiang, after signing the "State-owned Land Use Rights Reservation Agreement" in August 2001, gave Yu Zhijun a shopping card worth RMB 30,000. In January 2003, Yu Zhijun extorted RMB 330,000 from Lu Guoqiang on the pretext of buying a car. Yu Zhijun's acceptance of bribes and extortion, taking advantage of his position as the then Director of the Laoshan District Land and Resources Bureau, constituted personal criminal acts, for which the relevant court has already held him criminally liable. The signing of the "State-owned Land Use Rights Reservation Agreement" and the "State-owned Land Use Rights Grant Contract" between the Laoshan District Land and Resources Bureau and Nantai Company was to specifically implement the investment attraction project of the Qingdao Municipal People's Government of Shandong Province. Although Yu Zhijun served as the Director of the Laoshan District Land and Resources Bureau at the time of signing the relevant agreements, he did not have the power or responsibility to decide whether to sign the relevant agreements and contracts. The fact that Yu Zhijun, as the then Director of the Laoshan District Land and Resources Bureau, extorted RMB 330,000 from the other party for car purchase after signing the relevant agreements cannot prove that the Laoshan District Land and Resources Bureau and Nantai Company acted in malicious collusion to harm state interests when signing the relevant state-owned land use rights reservation agreement and grant contract. There is no evidence to prove that the Laoshan District Land and Resources Bureau and Nantai Company engaged in malicious collusion harming state interests during the signing of the "State-owned Land Use Rights Grant Contract." Therefore, the Laoshan District Land and Resources Bureau's claim to invalidate the relevant state-owned land use rights grant contract on this ground is insufficiently supported by evidence and is not accepted.

Regarding whether the appraisal of the land involved in this case complied with relevant regulations. The Laoshan District Land and Resources Bureau claimed that when handling public reports about this case, it commissioned Qingdao Hengyuan Appraisal Co., Ltd. to appraise the land under this case with August 13, 2002, as the base date. The appraised price differed significantly from the price appraised by Qingdao Eastern Real Estate Appraisal Consulting Co., Ltd., which served as the basis for the price in the grant contract. On this ground, it argued for the invalidity of the land use rights grant contract but did not raise objections to the appraisal qualifications of the appraisal institutions. The appraisal institution commissioned by Nantai Company conducted the appraisal with two land appraisers, which complied with relevant regulations. The land use purpose at the time of the appraisal commissioned by the Laoshan District Land and Resources Bureau was residential land, while the land use purpose at the time of the appraisal commissioned by Nantai Company before signing the grant contract was comprehensive land. Therefore, although the base date was the same (August 13, 2002), because the appraisal conclusions came from different appraisal institutions and appraisers, the appraisal times were different, and the land use purposes were different, significant differences in land appraisal prices could occur. The land use purpose agreed upon in the state-owned land use rights reservation agreement between the parties was comprehensive land, but the "Opinion Letter on the Review of Construction Engineering Planning" (Qing Gui Han Zi (2002) No. 84) issued by the Qingdao Municipal Planning Bureau of Shandong Province on February 4, 2002, indicated that, according to the overall planning of Shazikou Town approved by the Qingdao Municipal People's Government of Shandong Province, the planned nature of the project land was residential land, and the development nature was consistent with the planned nature of the land, so the site selection and construction were approved. Therefore, before the parties signed the "State-owned Land Use Rights Grant Contract," Nantai Company commissioned the appraisal with the land use purpose as comprehensive land. In the "State-owned Land Use Rights Grant Contract," the land use purpose was changed to residential land. This constituted a change in the content of certain clauses by the Laoshan District Land and Resources Bureau and Nantai Company through signing the contract, which does not conflict with the provision of Article 56 of the "Land Administration Law of the PRC" that when a construction unit uses state-owned land, it shall use the land in accordance with the provisions of the paid use contract such as the land use rights grant or the approved documents for the planning of the land use rights. If the inconsistency between the land use purpose in the "State-owned Land Use Rights Grant Contract" signed by the parties and that in the planning and appraisal report could potentially result in the land use rights grant price falling below the minimum price determined by the local government in accordance with state regulations at the time of signing the contract, it is a factor affecting the validity of the price clause of the state-owned land use rights grant contract, but does not render the state-owned land use rights grant contract invalid.

3. Regarding whether the first-instance judgment violated the civil litigation principle of "no trial without complaint." Upon examination, when Nantai Company read the first item of its complaint in court at the first instance requesting that the Laoshan District Land and Resources Bureau be ordered to continue performing the contract signed by the parties, it specifically clarified the substantive content of continuing performance of the contract, namely, handling the "State-owned Land Use Rights Certificate." This is corroborated by the first-instance trial transcript. According to Clause 2 of Article 15 of the "State-owned Land Use Rights Grant Contract" signed by the parties, the Laoshan District Land and Resources Bureau should, in accordance with the law, handle the grant land use rights registration for Nantai Company and issue the "State-owned Land Use Rights Certificate." This is a contractual obligation of the Laoshan District Land and Resources Bureau based on the "State-owned Land Use Rights Grant Contract" signed by the parties and falls within the scope of the obligation to continue performing the contract. The first-instance court's trial and judgment on this matter did not exceed the scope of civil adjudication and did not violate the civil litigation principle of "no trial without complaint."

After evaluating the three focal points of dispute of the parties mentioned above, this case also faces the issue of how to handle the "State-owned Land Use Rights Grant Contract" signed by the parties. Based on the allegations and defenses of the parties in the first-instance and second-instance trials of this case, the focal point of the parties' dispute has always revolved around the validity of the "State-owned Land Use Rights Grant Contract" involved in this case. In the situation where the court has confirmed, after trial, that the grounds put forward by the Laoshan District Land and Resources Bureau for arguing that the contract has not taken effect or is invalid are untenable, considering the specific circumstances of this case, there is also the issue of whether the contract rights and obligations should be terminated, or whether the contract should be rescinded. When engaging in civil activities, civil subjects must not only comply with the law but also observe state policies in the absence of legal provisions. According to relevant state regulations, if operational land was to be granted by agreement after July 1, 2002, without prior approval from the city or county government or a signed written project development agreement before that date, the grant should be changed to tender, auction, or listing methods in accordance with relevant regulations. The project land involved in this case only obtained project approval and did not obtain the "Construction Land Use Planning Permit" before July 1, 2002, which does not constitute a situation of prior approval. Before July 1, 2002, although the parties signed a joint construction contract and a state-owned land use rights reservation agreement, they did not sign a written project development agreement. Therefore, the disputed land in this case does not fall within the scope of historical issues that can be granted by agreement as determined by relevant state regulations. Nantai Company's request at the first instance for the court to order the Laoshan District Land and Resources Bureau to continue performing the "State-owned Land Use Rights Grant Contract" and immediately issue the state-owned land use rights certificate to Nantai Company is subject to the requirement that the disputed state-owned land use rights need to be granted by tender, auction, or listing methods in accordance with relevant state regulations, which is a state policy requirement. The failure of the Laoshan District Land and Resources Bureau to strictly implement the relevant state policy of granting the disputed land use rights through tender, auction, or listing methods was the reason for the impossibility of continuing performance of the "State-owned Land Use Rights Grant Contract" signed by the parties. Although this procedural requirement of policy does not render the "State-owned Land Use Rights Grant Contract" involved in this case invalid, it does affect the objective impossibility of continuing performance of the contract. Therefore, Nantai Company's claim for an order that the Laoshan District Land and Resources Bureau continue performing the "State-owned Land Use Rights Grant Contract" is difficult to support. The relevant items in the first-instance judgment should be reversed, and Nantai Company's claim on this matter should be dismissed. According to the spirit of relevant legal provisions, the right of rescission is a formative right in substantive terms and manifests as a formative action in procedural terms. In the absence of a party filing such a claim in accordance with the law, a people's court cannot ex officio make a ruling. The issue of rescission or termination of rights and obligations regarding the "State-owned Land Use Rights Grant Contract" and the assumption of legal liability arising therefrom need to be protected through an independent claim. In this case, Nantai Company has never raised a claim on this issue. Limited by the claims of the parties in this case and the scope of trial in the second-instance case, this court will not hear this issue.

In summary, the grounds for appeal raised by the Laoshan District Land and Resources Bureau that the "State-owned Land Use Rights Grant Contract" involved in this case has not taken effect or is invalid are untenable, and its grounds for arguing that the first-instance judgment violated civil litigation principles are also untenable. Because the "State-owned Land Use Rights Grant Contract" signed by the parties is in fact impossible to continue performing, Nantai Company's claim for an order requiring its continued performance is difficult to support. The relevant items in the first-instance judgment should be reversed, and Nantai Company's claim on this matter should be dismissed. The issue of whether the "State-owned Land Use Rights Grant Contract" involved in this case should be rescinded in accordance with the law and the assumption of legal consequences arising therefrom can be separately resolved by the parties in accordance with the law. Since the fundamental reason for the dispute between the parties and the failure of Nantai Company's claim for continued performance of the contract is caused by the conduct of the Laoshan District Land and Resources Bureau, the Laoshan District Land and Resources Bureau should bear the litigation costs, i.e., bear all the litigation costs of this case. Pursuant to Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (3) of the "Civil Procedure Law of the PRC," the judgment is as follows:

1. Reverse the civil judgment (2004) Lu Min Yi Chu Zi No. 9 of the Shandong High People's Court;

2. Dismiss the claim of Qingdao Nantai Real Estate Co., Ltd. for continued performance of the contract. The first-instance case acceptance fee, property preservation fee, and second-instance case acceptance fee, totaling RMB 865,569.16, shall be borne by the Laoshan District Land and Resources Bureau of Qingdao City.

This judgment is final.
